Tuition fees
As an international graduate researcher, you may be offered a Graduate Research Fee Offset Scholarship to offset your tuition fees, or you may enrol in a fee-paying place.
It’s important you read and understand the University’s current Tuition fee terms and conditions before accepting your offer and enrolling.
About graduate research scholarships
The University of Melbourne offers generous and comprehensive scholarship opportunities to recognise talent and support international graduate researchers. If you apply for a graduate research course, you'll be automatically considered for a range of scholarships. However, some scholarships require a separate application.
All international students who apply to a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree at the University of Melbourne will be automatically considered for Graduate Research Stipend and Fee Offset Scholarships.
If accepted to the course, you'll be exempt from paying tuition fees for your course. This exemption is valid for up to four years if you're enrolled in a doctoral program and up to two years if you're enrolled in a Masters by Research course.
International fee place
The majority of our international graduate researchers receive a tuition fee-remission scholarship.
However, if you choose to enrol in additional courses or subjects that are not related to your graduate research studies, you may incur additional costs such as tuition fees (if it's an International fee-paying place). Learn about additional coursework subjects.
For those not on a tuition-fee remission scholarship, tuition fee details are available below.
Tuition fee tables for International students
Previous years' tuition fees
Tuition fees are set annually, and are calculated on a daily basis for every day that you're enrolled (excluding any approved leave of absence) until you submit your thesis, or your enrolment ceases due to withdrawal or termination of enrolment.
Accept your offer and (if applicable) pay a deposit
Details about accepting your offer will be in your offer letter.
As part of accepting your offer and securing your place:
Most international graduate researchers receive a full tuition fee-remission scholarship. However, if you do not receive a tuition fee offset scholarship, you need to pay a minimum deposit of AUD$17,000. The deposit will be deducted from your remaining tuition fees.
If you choose for the University to arrange your Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), you also pay for OSHC when accepting your offer.
Fee payments
For graduate researchers, tuition fees are charged on a daily pro-rata basis during the period of your enrolment. Depending on the payment option you choose, you will receive an invoice either once or twice per semester for each day you are enrolled in research Semester 1 (1 January–30 June) and research Semester 2 (1 July–31 December).
If you're attending the University on a fee-remission scholarship, you'll be provided with a statement that shows the tuition fee amount charged for a specific calendar year and the amount sponsored or covered by your scholarship.
If you're a commencing graduate researcher who enrols after the research semester commencement date, your first research semester fees will be adjusted to take into account the number of days you will actually be enrolled in that semester. Similarly, once you submit your thesis, any refund of fees paid in advance will be calculated on a daily pro-rata basis.
Once you've completed your enrolment, an invoice for the balance of your tuition fees for the semester (or study period) will be available through the student portal – and you’ll need to pay your outstanding tuition fees by the due date.
You can pay your tuition fees through CIBC foreign exchange (pay in your home currency), credit card, BPAY® or telegraphic transfer.
Other fees and expenses
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
You're required to take out compulsory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) as a condition of your visa. You need to have this in place for the duration of your stay. This will cover any medical treatment or emergency care needed when in Australia.
If you receive a Graduate Research Scholarship, you'll receive an OSHC allowance covering your single membership. If you require a family membership to cover any dependents on your visa, you will need to pay for the difference.
Study and living expenses
You'll need to consider additional costs, fees, and other incidental expenses related to your studies, such as administrative charges or materials and resources. While most research-related costs are covered, some non‑tuition fees may still apply, refer to the Tuition fee terms and conditions for details on non‑tuition fees.
Visit Accommodation to find out about housing options and costs.
Student Services and Amenities Fee
International students don't pay a Student Services and Amenities Fee (SSAF), this is covered by the University.
Funding support and scholarships
As an international graduate researcher, you may be offered a Graduate Research Scholarship to assist with living expenses.
There are other scholarships and bursaries that can help you pay tuition fees and living expenses.
We offer over 1,200 scholarships and bursaries. Some cover part or all of your course fees, and others are one-off grants. Search Scholarships.
Visit Support and Wellbeing for advice on student loans, hardship grants and other support.
The University also supports applicants who receive scholarship support from other funders. If you're applying for an external scholarship, this should be detailed in your application.
